title: Decommission and Data Rotation Security Playbook
author: Priya Menon
content:
Summary
This playbook documents the security-safe decommission and data rotation process for Redwood services and supporting systems. It combines RBAC revocation steps, audit logging and evidence collection requirements, data retention matrix updates, secure deletion and key-management patterns, and incident handling guidance for decommission windows. The goal is to ensure regulatory alignment (GDPR, SOC2 Evidence), preserve necessary audit artifacts, and safely remove access and data across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope
- Applies to decommission of services, environments, storage buckets, model artifacts, logging indices, and service accounts associated with: artifact-store, model-registry, s3-retention-bucket, redis-kv-caches, and ephemeral inference logs.
- Does NOT replace tenant offboarding or legal holds; see Legal Hold procedure before starting.

Definitions
- Data Rotation: periodic overwrite/removal of old records per retention matrix.
- Decommission: final shutdown and removal of a resource (VM, bucket, index, or service).
- Evidence Package: exported audit records, manifests, and checksums required for regulatory audits.

Prerequisites and Safety Checks
1) Verify there are no active legal holds: run: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood/legal-holds?env=<env> and confirm zero holds.
2) Confirm owner sign-off: a ticket in JIRA with approval from data-owner and product-owner is required (JIRA project: INF-SEC).
3) Snapshot essential artifacts: manifest of artifact-store snapshot (sha256 checksums) and model-registry version map.
4) Ensure backup retention policy is compatible with target retention window and compliance requirements.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Requestor: raises the decommission ticket and validates service-level prechecks.
- Data Owner: approves retention decisions and legal hold checks.
- Security Engineer (owner): runs RBAC revocation, audit export, evidence packaging.
- Infra SRE: executes infrastructure teardown and ensures secure deletion.
- Compliance: signs the final evidence package and retention update.

SLOs and Timelines
- Pre-decommission window: 5 business days for approvals and evidence exports.
- RBAC revocation: immediate (within 2 hours of start) for non-production secrets; within 24 hours for production service accounts when a staged rollback is required.
- Evidence packaging delivery: within 48 hours of decommission.

Step-by-step Decommission Procedure
1) Ticket and Approval
  - Create JIRA INF-SEC ticket with: list of resources, data-owner, product-owner, KMS key IDs, and proposed deletion date.
  - Attach retention matrix decision and legal-hold verification.
2) Pre-Export Audit Snapshot
  - Export authz logs for 90 days (or configured retention) from audit-elasticsearch:
    - curl -XPOST "https://audit.internal/api/export" -d '{"index":"authz-*","range":"last_90_days","format":"ndjson"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EXPORT_TOKEN' > authz-90d.ndjson
  - Run access-list report for affected resources: python tools/access_report.py --resource <resource-id> --output access-report.csv
3) RBAC Revocation (IdP + IAM)
  - Break down changes in two phases: revoke user access first, archive group bindings, then rotate service principals.
  - User access: remove users/groups in IdP (Okta) and confirm via SCIM sync. Example Okta CLI: okta apps deassign --app <app-id> --group <group-id>
  - Service principals: create replacement principal if needed, and rotate keys before deletion. For GCP: gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete <KEY_ID> --iam-account=<SA>@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  - Update RBAC audit table: INSERT row in decommission_audit with action="rbac-revoked", actor, timestamp, resource. (Operations team will run the insert using internal tooling.)
4) Quarantine and Read-Only Phase (optional for high-risk resources)
  - Switch buckets/indexes to read-only: s3 lifecycle rule or elasticsearch index block write API.
  - Monitor error rates and service telemetry for 48 hours.
5) Evidence Packaging and Hashing
  - Package exported logs, access reports, manifests into an evidence bundle. Provide checksums: sha256sum evidence-bundle.tar.gz > evidence-bundle.sha256
  - Store evidence in evidence-collector (WORM storage) with metadata including JIRA ticket ID, retention classification, and approver: curl -XPUT https://evidence-collector.internal/store -F file=@evidence-bundle.tar.gz -F metadata='{"ticket":"INF-SEC-1234","classification":"audit","approver":"Priya Menon"}'
6) Secure Deletion and Key Rotation
  - For object storage: over-write sensitive objects using rotational deletes where required and then run bucket-level permanent delete after WORM retention expiry.
  - For KMS: schedule key destruction per KMS policy. Before schedule, rotate keys for any dependent services and revoke access.
  - Perform NIST SP 800-88 compliant wipe for on-prem disks where applicable; document wipe tool and serial numbers in evidence bundle.
7) Verification and Post-Deletion Audit
  - Verify resource absence with automated scans: tools/inventory-scan --resource <id> --assert-absent
  - Run a post-decommission report and attach to the JIRA ticket.
  - Compliance signs off and sets final retention on evidence package.

Data Rotation Schedule and Retention Matrix (sample)
- Log type: inference-audit (token-level) | Retention: 90 days | Action: rotate to cold-tier after 30 days, then delete after 90 days
- Log type: authz-events | Retention: 7 years (for regulated customers) | Action: export to evidence-collector and index-archive (WORM)
- Artifact: model-checkpoint | Retention: 1 year | Action: snapshot + move to cold-store; delete after 1 year unless flagged by legal hold
- Backup snapshot: infra-backup | Retention: 30 days | Action: incremental rotation, purge older snapshots daily maintenance

RBAC Considerations (detailed)
- Principle of least privilege: any user/service not explicitly required for the decommission workflow must be removed from associated groups before teardown starts.
- Temporary elevated roles: use JIT (just-in-time) elevation and ensure time-bound bindings with automatic revocation (Okta PCE and internal-timebound-service).
- Evidence: capture the before/after membership of all groups that lost access and include as CSV in evidence bundle.

Audit Logging & Evidence Requirements
- Minimum audit window to export: 90 days for standard operations, 7 years when regulatory obligations require it.
- Logs to include: authn/authz events, KMS key operations, account provisioning, object delete events, index deletion in search clusters, and tenant-aware access traces.
- Anti-tamper: store exported audits to evidence-collector with checksum and attestations, and record the storage location in the JIRA ticket.

Automations and Tooling
- inventory-scan: verifies presence/absence of resources across clouds.
- access_report.py: enumerates principals with bindings to given resource.
- evidence-collector CLI: redwood-evidence upload --file evidence-bundle.tar.gz --ticket INF-SEC-1234
- retention-sync job: updates retention matrix in the metadata DB.

Incident Playbook (if issues arise during decommission)
1) Scenario: Unexpected access detected post-revocation\  - Immediate action: re-instate quarantine and rotate any compromised keys.
  - Forensics: snapshot current authz logs (append-only) and escalate to Incident Response (pager: #sec-ir).
  - Communicate: update the INF-SEC ticket with findings and schedule a hot review within 2 business hours.
2) Scenario: Evidence bundle mismatch (checksum failure)\  - Re-export the raw logs and re-run packaging. If discrepancies continue, preserve both bundles and create an evidence integrity exception for Compliance.

Verification Checklist (to attach to JIRA)
- [ ] Legal hold check completed and attached
- [ ] Data owner sign-off obtained
- [ ] Authz logs exported and checksum verified
- [ ] RBAC revocations recorded and CSV attached
- [ ] Evidence bundle stored in WORM with metadata
- [ ] KMS keys rotated/scheduled for destruction or archived per policy
- [ ] Inventory scan confirms resource absence
- [ ] Compliance sign-off (name + date)

Appendix: Example CLI snippets and SQL queries
- Export access list (SQL):
  SELECT principal, binding, resource, granted_at FROM rbac_bindings WHERE resource_id = '<resource-id>' AND revoked_at IS NULL;
- Example s3 lifecycle to set read-only (AWS CLI):
  aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket my-bucket --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled
  aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket my-bucket --lifecycle-configuration file://lifecycle.json
- Evidence checksum: sha256sum evidence-bundle.tar.gz > evidence-bundle.sha256
